source.title: Special Delivery: How One Box Cuts Packaging in Half
source.section: Nike 官方产品包装创新案例
source.type: Nike 官方产品包装创新案例
source.context: Nike 官方公开业务资料。
paragraphs: "It was meant to be a limited release. So we said, 'Let's be daring and try something we're not sure is going to work'", says Rich of the sneaker collection that was delivered in its own oblong shoe box. "But the shoes were so popular, we had to scale up and fast. We got a lot of feedback that the box wasn't durable enough to withstand the rigours of delivery, so we got to work updating it based on those learnings".

Rich and team ran a battery of engineering exercises, like crush tests that beat up the box, to make sure it would survive the journey to your door. Those tests helped the team build an even stronger container—and proved that the design could work on a way bigger scale. The result of dreaming and testing big? Nike One Box. This current design can house almost any shoe Nike makes. And although it may look different from the box that started it all, its intent is the same: reduce waste. Delivering shoes in their shoe box and ditching the outer box (plus any extra packaging) add up to big wins.

Does this mean One Box is going to replace all existing shoe boxes? No, not right away. Millions of units are being delivered this year and that number is only expected to grow through meticulous testing and refinement. "Even though it's large, we're still in pilot mode", says Erica. "There's opportunity for One Box to evolve over time—how it looks, what it's used for and how many boxes we can save". And just as Space Hippie inspired this game-changing container, One Box is sparking new ideas for changing other packaging practices. For example, reducing the amount of paper used to stuff the toes of shoes or doing away with the plastic bags that encase individual apparel items. Rich notes that it's part of a bigger story: Nike's overall push to reduce product packaging, an effort that is constantly evolving.
translations: 我们原本计划限量推出这款鞋。我们决定大胆尝试一种尚不确定是否可行的方案。鞋款很受欢迎后，必须迅速扩大规模。我们收到很多反馈，认为鞋盒不够结实，无法承受运输过程，于是根据这些经验着手改进。
Rich 和团队进行了多轮工程测试，例如反复挤压盒子，确认它能经受运送到顾客家门的过程。这些测试帮助团队做出更坚固的包装，也证明该设计可以扩大应用。经过大胆构想和充分测试，Nike One Box 诞生了。当前设计几乎可以装下 Nike 生产的任何鞋款。虽然外观与最初的鞋盒不同，目标仍然是减少浪费：直接用鞋盒寄送鞋子，省去外层纸箱和其他额外包装，就能显著减少包装材料。

这是否意味着 One Box 会立即取代所有现有鞋盒？不会。尽管今年已有数百万件商品使用这种包装，预计这一数字还会增长，但这依赖于持续、细致的测试和改进。负责人 Erica 说：“即使现在规模已经不小，我们仍处于试点阶段。One Box 还有继续发展的空间，包括外观、用途，以及还能节省多少包装。”正如 Space Hippie 启发了这种创新包装，One Box 也带来了改进其他包装方式的新想法，例如减少鞋头填充用纸，或取消单件服装外面的塑料袋。Rich 表示，这属于 Nike 持续减少产品包装的整体行动，而这项工作仍在不断推进。
fullTextParagraphs: Learn how Nike's packaging team is ditching the double box to help reduce waste—and re-imagining what a shoe box can do.
Presented by Move to Zero: Nike's Journey towards zero carbon and zero waste to help protect the future of sport.

"Packaging is sometimes an afterthought", says Rich Hastings, the mastermind behind Nike's custom shoe-box designs for more than 20 years. "But what people may not realise is that it can have a huge impact on the environment". You may have noticed that impact when the shoes you bought online arrive in their shoe box, surrounded by another box. "We knew we had the opportunity to make our existing model better", he says. Rich and team had the chance to do just that when they worked on the 2020 release of Space Hippie—a line of shoes made from at least 25 percent to 50 percent recycled material by weight that needed an audaciously low-impact container to match their future-focused design.
Rich Hastings helped bring One Box to life after working on the Space Hippie box (centre), which ditched the box within a box we're all familiar with.

"Space Hippie was the jumping off point", says Erica Swanson from sustainable product operations. "We wanted to have an innovative system that delivered a shoe in its own container, rather than delivering a box within another box". So when you buy one pair of shoes online, this eliminates an entire box from your order—and your recycling bin. Sounds simple, but like any industry-leading concept, it would take a lot of work to bring to fruition.

"It was meant to be a limited release. So we said, 'Let's be daring and try something we're not sure is going to work'", says Rich of the sneaker collection that was delivered in its own oblong shoe box. "But the shoes were so popular, we had to scale up and fast. We got a lot of feedback that the box wasn't durable enough to withstand the rigours of delivery, so we got to work updating it based on those learnings".

Erica Swanson is helping take Nike to new heights with One Box. "We learnt that 86 percent of consumers said they would like to work with brands to make them more sustainable", says Erica. "With One Box, we deliver on this need".

Rich and team ran a battery of engineering exercises, like crush tests that beat up the box, to make sure it would survive the journey to your door. Those tests helped the team build an even stronger container—and proved that the design could work on a way bigger scale. The result of dreaming and testing big? Nike One Box. This current design can house almost any shoe Nike makes. And although it may look different from the box that started it all, its intent is the same: reduce waste. Delivering shoes in their shoe box and ditching the outer box (plus any extra packaging) add up to big wins.
How do you make a box into a breakthrough? According to Chris Conklin, it comes down to obsessing over the details.
"Our team worked together to really obsess over how the customer would interact with the box", says Chris Conklin from packaging design. Take a tour through the result of all that detailed work:

Stealthy Exterior From afar, One Box might seem underwhelming—but that's the whole point. "It was a strategic choice for security", says Chris of the logo-free design. "We didn't want the box advertising that new shoes were sitting on your doorstep".

Tape-Free Returns The lid of the box is secured with an adhesive strip to cut down on tape waste. But sometimes things don't work out, so the team knew they also had to solve how shoppers would handle returns. That's why they added a second strip of adhesive that lets you reseal the box and return the shoes.

No-Smudge Graphics "We tried using different colours for graphics inside the box", says Chris. "But when we noticed the ink rubbed off on white midsoles, we switched to white to keep the product perfect". And how we applied that white ink stayed true to the overall mission of reducing waste. "We were thinking about water use when printing", says Chris. "We wanted the design to be minimal enough that we could keep the overall footprint low".

If One Box shows up on your door, you'll see these features come to life on this shoe-box-delivery-container combo. You may also see a scuff or two. "Think of these as reminders that you helped remove an extra box from the recycling bin", suggests Erica.

Does this mean One Box is going to replace all existing shoe boxes? No, not right away. Millions of units are being delivered this year and that number is only expected to grow through meticulous testing and refinement. "Even though it's large, we're still in pilot mode", says Erica. "There's opportunity for One Box to evolve over time—how it looks, what it's used for and how many boxes we can save". And just as Space Hippie inspired this game-changing container, One Box is sparking new ideas for changing other packaging practices. For example, reducing the amount of paper used to stuff the toes of shoes or doing away with the plastic bags that encase individual apparel items. Rich notes that it's part of a bigger story: Nike's overall push to reduce product packaging, an effort that is constantly evolving.
Erica Swanson Senior Director, Sustainable Product Operations
For more: Visit Nike.com/Sustainability to follow each step in our journey and discover new ways we can Move to Zero carbon and zero waste together.

scenario.title: 模拟情境：新包装减少材料，但试点中出现破损
english: The new package uses less material, but several boxes were damaged during delivery in the first pilot.
The product team updated the design and ran additional crush tests.
Summarize the feedback and test results, then recommend whether to expand the pilot.
chinese: 新包装使用的材料更少，但首轮试点中有几只盒子在配送时受损。
产品团队调整设计，并进行了额外的挤压测试。
请概括反馈和测试结果，再建议是否扩大试点范围。

firstAttempt.prompt: 请向项目负责人汇报新包装试点：说明收到的运输破损反馈、团队做了什么调整和测试，并提出下一步建议。
firstAttempt.sample: The first pilot reduced packaging, but we received feedback that the box wasn’t durable enough for delivery. We strengthened the design and ran additional crush tests. The results were positive, so I recommend expanding the pilot to another region and tracking damage rates before a full rollout.
firstAttempt.rationale: 按反馈、调整、测试结果和建议的顺序汇报。

words.translation: 改进后的包装足够结实，可以用于配送。

words.example: We’ll run a pilot in two regions before expanding the service.

words.translation: 这款产品还需要进一步测试和改进。

choice.prompt: 试点发现包装破损率偏高，团队加固后又做了测试。哪种汇报最完整？
options: The first box was bad, but this one is good.

The new box looks better, so we should launch everywhere.

output.prompt: 你负责的客户服务流程试点缩短了响应时间，但一个地区仍有较多漏单。请说明团队根据反馈修改了提醒流程，测试结果有所改善，并建议在扩大前继续跟踪漏单率。
output.sample: The pilot reduced response time, but one region still had missed requests. We updated the reminder process based on team feedback, and the retest showed improvement. I recommend continuing to track missed requests at the current scale before deciding whether to expand.
